headline: ENERGYX SEALS $2B, 10-YEAR LITHIUM DEAL WITH TRAFIGURA — CHILE AND TEXAS PROJECTS LAND ANCHOR BUYER BEFORE FIRST TONNE PRODUCED
snippet: EnergyX announced on October 12 a binding 10-year take-or-pay offtake agreement with commodity trader Trafigura for 100,000 metric tonnes of battery-grade lithium products, representing approximately $2 billion in revenue at current prices of ~$20,000/t. Supply comes from EnergyX's Black Giant direct lithium extraction project in Chile (lithium carbonate, 66% of Phase 1 offtake) and its Lonestar project in Texas (lithium hydroxide, 30% of Phase 1), with production targeted from 2028–2029. The deal supports EnergyX's $690 million US Export-Import Bank loan application and is among the largest pre-production DLE offtake agreements signed to date — a rare vote of confidence in American lithium supply chain development at a moment when Chinese spot prices are at 10-month lows.

headline: CODELCO CONFIRMS 2 DEAD AFTER AVALANCHE AT EL TENIENTE — SECOND FATAL ACCIDENT AT WORLD'S LARGEST UNDERGROUND COPPER MINE IN 15 MONTHS
snippet: A snow avalanche struck the open-pit area of Codelco's El Teniente copper mine in Chile on October 11, killing two contract workers from subcontractor Aura. A third worker was rescued. Operations in the affected pit — supplying under 10% of mine output — were suspended while underground mining and processing continue. The accident is El Teniente's second deadly incident in fifteen months, following a July 2025 underground collapse that killed six workers. The fatalities add to a widening Chilean copper supply-risk picture already strained by simultaneous labour disputes at Centinela and Escondida.

headline: CHILE COPPER CRUNCH DEEPENS: CENTINELA HUNGER STRIKERS CAMP IN SANTIAGO, BHP ESCONDIDA MEDIATION DECLARED DEAD
snippet: Chile's copper sector entered a simultaneous two-front labour crisis by October 9. At Antofagasta's Centinela mine (~700,000 t/yr), three union leaders began a hunger strike while roughly 50 members camped in Santiago's financial district after government mediation failed to close an equal-pay gap. At BHP's Escondida — the world's single largest copper mine at over 1 million t/yr — supervisors' union president Alexis Barrera told Reuters on October 9 that government mediation had produced "no progress" after four days. BMO analysts project output impacts could emerge in November if no settlement is reached. LME copper gained ~1% on October 9 to approximately $14,615/t on supply-risk concerns.

headline: ZIMBABWE TELLS LITHIUM PRODUCERS: "NO REASON" TO DELAY JANUARY 2027 EXPORT BAN — TIME'S UP ON UNPROCESSED CONCENTRATE SHIPMENTS
snippet: Zimbabwe's Information Minister Nick Mangwana confirmed around October 9 that there is "no reason" to delay the country's ban on lithium concentrate exports, due to take effect January 1, 2027, dismissing producers' requests for more time. Miners were told they have had "ample time" to establish local processing facilities, as required under the Ministry of Mines framework issued in April. A 10% export tax on concentrates is already in force pending the full ban. Fitch's BMI projects the policy will tighten ex-China lithium supply from Q1 2027 through at least mid-to-late 2027 — a potential floor under depressed prices at a time when Chinese domestic futures are at 10-month lows near US$15,900/t.

headline: MONEY METALS PODCAST: WELDON SAYS GOLD'S REBOUND IS JUST BEGINNING — WASHINGTON'S FISCAL RECKLESSNESS IS "STEALING" FUTURE RETURNS
snippet: In a Money Metals Exchange podcast dated October 9, veteran macro analyst Greg Weldon argues that gold's current rebound from the September correction marks the resumption — not the end — of the structural bull market. Weldon says Washington's persistent deficit spending is the "gold thief": monetising debt erodes real returns on bonds and cash, structurally boosting the long-term case for gold to $8,500–$10,000/oz over a three-year horizon. His near-term caution is reflected in trading-model sell signals, but he says he is not betting against gold because the macro foundation built by rising debt and a weakening dollar is more durable than any short-term technical correction.

headline: GOLD SWOT: TOREX BEATS Q3 GUIDANCE, FORTUNA SLIPS ON SÉGUÉLA, B2GOLD GOOSE MINE ADDS CRUSHING CAPACITY
snippet: Frank Holmes' weekly Gold SWOT analysis for October 12 highlights Torex Gold (TSX: TXG) as a strength — producing 131,900 oz AuEq in Q3 at Media Luna running 10% above design-rate throughput and tracking toward the guidance midpoint of 420,000–470,000 oz AuEq. On the weakness side, Fortuna Mining's Séguéla mine slipped to 33,744 oz in Q3 from 41,683 oz in Q2, hurt by contractor equipment shortages and an artisanal mining blockade; full-year guidance of 281,000–305,000 GEO remains intact at the lower end. B2Gold is expanding crushing capacity at its Goose Mine in Nunavut. The week's broader theme: operational execution remains the primary differentiator for gold producers in a flat-to-declining gold price environment.

headline: LUCA MINING CEO: $385M COZAMIN DEAL PLUS BARQUEÑO ACQUISITION TRANSFORMS JUNIOR INTO MULTI-MINE POLYMETALLIC PRODUCER
snippet: Crux Investor's October 9 CEO interview with Luca Mining (TSX-V: LUCA) covers both deals defining the company's next phase: the up-to-US$385 million acquisition of Capstone Copper's Cozamin polymetallic mine in Zacatecas (expected to close Q4 2026, more than doubling 2027 production) and the acquisition of Agnico Eagle's El Barqueño property in Mexico. Together, the transactions transform Luca from a single-asset junior into a multi-mine copper-gold-silver producer with exploration upside at both assets. Financing includes a bought deal led by National Bank with strategic participation from Wheaton Precious Metals and Taurus — the structure ensuring Luca enters its growth phase with a royalty partner aligned on upside.

headline: WORLD GOLD COUNCIL TELLS MINERS: NAME YOUR REFINERS PUBLICLY OR RISK SUPPLY CHAIN STIGMA
snippet: The World Gold Council issued new disclosure guidance asking all producers of doré to publish an annual list tying each mine to its refining partners and their countries of operation, as part of an escalating supply chain transparency push. The framework follows a 2023 commitment by WGC's 33 member companies — representing roughly 1,300 tonnes of annual production — and coincides with new LBMA rules effective January 2026 requiring refiners to disclose WGC-member mine sources. The initiative was accelerated by reporting on suspect gold flows and the Royal Canadian Mint's expanded sourcing disclosures. For junior explorers targeting eventual off-take with major refiners, the disclosure trend raises early-stage governance expectations.

headline: GENESIS GOLD WEIGHS MINE SALES AFTER VAULT MINERALS TAKEOVER CLOSES — A$12.6B MERGER TRIGGERS ASSET RATIONALIZATION
snippet: Genesis Minerals (ASX: GMD) is actively evaluating the sale of non-core gold mines following the completion of its A$12.6 billion takeover of Vault Minerals — the largest gold sector merger in Australia's history. Management indicated post-merger integration requires concentrating capital on the combined company's highest-quality assets, with divestiture of lower-priority operations expected to fund growth and reduce debt. The consolidation follows the broader 2026 trend of major gold M&A activity (Equinox-Orla, Discovery-Newmont Porcupine assets), and the potential asset sales could create junior acquisition opportunities in Australian gold as the combined entity streamlines.
